title: Second-order systems and applications
lead: Masses joined by springs between walls give a second-order system $\kM\kvecxdprime = \kK\kvecx$, which the section treats as it stands rather than as a first-order one. It solves the undamped system with eigenvalues and eigenvectors, follows two carts on springs and two coupled rail cars, and then adds periodic forcing and asks when resonance occurs.
notes: The section notes (the lecture count and the [EP] section number) are left out.
exercises_lead: Exercises with numbers 101 and higher have solutions.
exercise_notes: Bloom levels and concept tags are AI-generated. Exercises 3.6.101–3.6.103 carry the book’s own answers, each confirmed by computation. assumes.text: The derivative of $e^{\kalpha t}$ is $\kalpha e^{\kalpha t}$, and $\kvecv$ is a constant vector, so each derivative brings out one factor of $\kalpha$.
$e^{\kalpha t}$ is never zero, so we may divide by it.

assumes.text: The derivative of $\cos(\komega t)$ is $-\komega \sin(\komega t)$ and that of $\sin(\komega t)$ is $\komega \cos(\komega t)$; $\kvecc$ is a constant vector.
The equation holds for every $t$, so the vectors multiplying $\cos(\komega t)$ on the two sides are equal.
$\komega$ is not a natural frequency, so $-\komega^2$ is not an eigenvalue of $\kA$ and $\kA + \komega^2 \kI$ is invertible.

steps.cap: Multiply both sides on the left by ${(\kA + \komega^2 \kI)}^{-1}$, which cancels the matrix in front of $\kvecc$.

exercises.prompt: Repeat this setup for 4 masses (find the matrices $\kM$ and $\kK$). Do it for 5 masses. Can you find a prescription to do it for $n$ masses?

answer.solution: With $n$ masses there are $n + 1$ springs, spring $i$ on the left of mass $i$ and spring $i+1$ on its right, with the walls at $x_0 = x_{n+1} = 0$. Hooke’s law gives mass $i$ the force $-k_i(x_i - x_{i-1}) + k_{i+1}(x_{i+1} - x_i) = k_i x_{i-1} - (k_i + k_{i+1}) x_i + k_{i+1} x_{i+1}$. So $\kM$ is diagonal with $m_1, \ldots, m_n$ on the diagonal, and $\kK$ is tridiagonal: $K_{ii} = -(k_i + k_{i+1})$, $K_{i,i+1} = K_{i+1,i} = k_{i+1}$, every other entry $0$. For 4 masses, $\kM = \left[ \begin{smallmatrix} m_1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & m_2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & m_3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & m_4 \end{smallmatrix} \right]$ and $\kK = \left[ \begin{smallmatrix} -(k_1+k_2) & k_2 & 0 & 0 \\ k_2 & -(k_2+k_3) & k_3 & 0 \\ 0 & k_3 & -(k_3+k_4) & k_4 \\ 0 & 0 & k_4 & -(k_4+k_5) \end{smallmatrix} \right]$. For 5 masses, $\kM$ is diagonal with $m_1, \ldots, m_5$ and $\kK = \left[ \begin{smallmatrix} -(k_1+k_2) & k_2 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ k_2 & -(k_2+k_3) & k_3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & k_3 & -(k_3+k_4) & k_4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & k_4 & -(k_4+k_5) & k_5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & k_5 & -(k_5+k_6) \end{smallmatrix} \right]$. Multiplying out $\kK\kvecx$ for 4 masses gives back the four force sums, row by row.

exercises.prompt: Show that if $\kA$ has a zero eigenvalue and $\kvecv$ is a corresponding eigenvector, then $\kvecx = \kvecv (a + bt)$ is a solution of $\kvecxdprime = \kA \kvecx$ for arbitrary constants $a$ and $b$.

answer.solution: Differentiate twice: $\kvecxprime = b\kvecv$ and $\kvecxdprime = \vec{0}$, since $\kvecv$, $a$ and $b$ are constants. On the other side, $\kA\kvecx = (a + bt)\kA\kvecv = (a + bt)\, 0\, \kvecv = \vec{0}$, because $\kA\kvecv = 0\kvecv$ for an eigenvector of the eigenvalue 0. Both sides are $\vec{0}$ for every $t$, so $\kvecx = \kvecv(a + bt)$ solves $\kvecxdprime = \kA\kvecx$ for any $a$ and $b$.

$\kvecxp = \left[ \begin{smallmatrix} -1/6 \\ 1/6 \end{smallmatrix} \right] t \sin(2t) + \left[ \begin{smallmatrix} -2/3 \\ 0 \end{smallmatrix} \right] \cos(2t)$ (any multiple of $\left[ \begin{smallmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \end{smallmatrix} \right] \cos(2t)$ may be added). This is the matrix of Example 3.6.1, whose natural frequencies are 1 and 2, so $\komega = 2$ is a natural frequency: $\kA + 4\kI = \left[ \begin{smallmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 2 \end{smallmatrix} \right]$ is not invertible and we must try $\kvecxp = \kvecc\, t\sin(2t) + \kvecd \cos(2t)$. Then $\kvecxpdprime = \kvecc\,(4\cos(2t) - 4t\sin(2t)) - 4\kvecd\cos(2t)$. Matching the $t\sin(2t)$ terms gives $(\kA + 4\kI)\kvecc = \vec{0}$, so $\kvecc = s\left[ \begin{smallmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \end{smallmatrix} \right]$, the eigenvector of $-4$. Matching the $\cos(2t)$ terms gives $(\kA + 4\kI)\kvecd = 4\kvecc - \left[ \begin{smallmatrix} 0 \\ 2 \end{smallmatrix} \right] = \left[ \begin{smallmatrix} 4s \\ -4s - 2 \end{smallmatrix} \right]$. The left side is $(d_1 + d_2)\left[ \begin{smallmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{smallmatrix} \right]$, so $-4s - 2 = 8s$, $s = -\frac{1}{6}$, and $d_1 + d_2 = -\frac{2}{3}$; take $d_2 = 0$. Substituting back confirms the solution.

exercises.prompt:
Consider the example in Figure 3.13 with the same parameters as before: $m_1 = 2$, $k_1 = 4$, and $k_2 = 2$, except for $m_2$, which is unknown. Suppose that there is a force $\cos (5 t)$ acting on the first mass. Find an $m_2$ such that there exists a particular solution where the first mass does not move.

Note: This idea is called dynamic damping. In practice there will be a small amount of damping and so any transient solution will disappear and after long enough time, the first mass will always come to a stop.

answer.solution: $m_2 = \frac{2}{25} = 0.08$ kg. Here $\kA = \kMinv\kK = \left[ \begin{smallmatrix} -3 & 1 \\ 2/m_2 & -2/m_2 \end{smallmatrix} \right]$ and $\kvecF = \kMinv \left[ \begin{smallmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{smallmatrix} \right] = \left[ \begin{smallmatrix} 1/2 \\ 0 \end{smallmatrix} \right]$. The guess $\kvecxp = \kvecc\cos(5t)$ needs $(\kA + 25\kI)\kvecc = -\kvecF$, that is, $22c_1 + c_2 = -\frac{1}{2}$ and $\frac{2}{m_2}c_1 + \left(25 - \frac{2}{m_2}\right)c_2 = 0$. For the first mass to stand still we need $c_1 = 0$; then $c_2 = -\frac{1}{2}$, and the second equation becomes $\left(25 - \frac{2}{m_2}\right)\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) = 0$, so $m_2 = \frac{2}{25}$. Then the second mass moves as $-\frac{1}{2}\cos(5t)$, and the spring $k_2$ pulls on the first mass with $2(x_2 - x_1) = -\cos(5t)$, exactly cancelling the force: the second mass on its spring alone has natural frequency $\sqrt{k_2/m_2} = 5$, the forcing frequency.

exercises.prompt:
Let us take the Example 3.6.2, but that at time of impact, car 2 is moving to the left with speed 3 m/s.

  1. Find the behavior of the system after linkup.
  2. Will the second car hit the wall, or will it be moving away from the wall as time goes on?
  3. At what speed would the first car have to be traveling for the system to essentially stay in place after linkup?

answer.solution: a) The general solution of Example 3.6.2 still holds, and $\kvecx(0) = \vec{0}$ still gives $a_1 = a_2 = 0$. Now $\kvecxprime(0) = \left[ \begin{smallmatrix} 3 \\ -3 \end{smallmatrix} \right]$, so $b_1 + \sqrt{3}\, b_2 = 3$ and $b_1 - 2\sqrt{3}\, b_2 = -3$, which give $b_2 = \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$ and $b_1 = 1$. Hence $\kvecx = \left[ \begin{smallmatrix} t + \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \sin(\sqrt{3}\, t) \\ t - \frac{4}{\sqrt{3}} \sin(\sqrt{3}\, t) \end{smallmatrix} \right]$: the pair drifts to the right at 1 m/s while the bumper makes the cars oscillate against each other at the frequency $\sqrt{3}$. b) It hits the wall. The term $b_1 t = t$ grows without bound, while the oscillation of $\kxtwo$ has amplitude only $\frac{4}{\sqrt{3}} \approx 2.31$. Car 2 first backs up to about $-1.48$ m, then is carried forward and reaches $\kxtwo = 10$ at $t \approx 9.26$ s, at about 4.79 m/s. c) The drift is $b_1 = \frac{2\kxoneprime(0) + \kxtwoprime(0)}{3}$ (solve the two equations for $b_1$), so the system stays in place when $2\kxoneprime(0) - 3 = 0$, that is, when the first car travels at $\frac{3}{2} = 1.5$ m/s. Then $b_1 = 0$, $b_2 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, and $\kvecx = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\sin(\sqrt{3}\, t) \left[ \begin{smallmatrix} 1 \\ -2 \end{smallmatrix} \right]$: the cars only oscillate about where they linked.

exercises.prompt: Let us take the example in Figure 3.13 with parameters $m_1 = m_2 = 1$, $k_1 = k_2 = 1$. Does there exist a set of initial conditions for which the first cart moves but the second cart does not? If so, find those conditions. If not, argue why not.

answer.solution: No. The system is $\kvecxdprime = \left[ \begin{smallmatrix} -2 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 \end{smallmatrix} \right] \kvecx$, whose second equation is $\kxtwodprime = \kxone - \kxtwo$. If the second cart never moves, $\kxtwo \equiv 0$, then $\kxtwodprime \equiv 0$ and the equation forces $\kxone \equiv 0$: the first cart cannot move either. Physically, a moving first cart stretches or squeezes the spring $k_2$, which then pushes the second cart. In terms of the modes, the eigenvalues are $\frac{-3 \pm \sqrt{5}}{2}$, both eigenvectors have a nonzero second entry, and no combination of the two modes with distinct frequencies keeps $\kxtwo$ at zero unless both are absent.

$\kvecx = \left[ \begin{smallmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \\ 1 \end{smallmatrix}\right] \bigl( a_1 \cos (\sqrt{3}\, t) + b_1 \sin (\sqrt{3}\, t) \bigr) + \left[ \begin{smallmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \\ -2 \end{smallmatrix}\right] \bigl( a_2 \cos (\sqrt{2}\, t) + b_2 \sin (\sqrt{2}\, t) \bigr) + \left[ \begin{smallmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{smallmatrix}\right] \bigl( a_3 \cos (t) + b_3 \sin (t) \bigr) + \left[ \begin{smallmatrix} -1 \\ {1}/{2} \\ {-1}/{3} \end{smallmatrix}\right] \cos (2t)$

exercises.prompt: Suppose there are three carts of equal mass $m$ and connected by two springs of constant $k$ (and no connections to walls). Set up the system and find its general solution.

answer.solution: $\left[ \begin{smallmatrix} m & 0 & 0\\ 0 & m & 0\\ 0 & 0 & m \end{smallmatrix}\right] \kvecxdprime = \left[ \begin{smallmatrix} -k & k & 0 \\ k & -2k & k \\ 0 & k & -k \end{smallmatrix}\right] \kvecx$. Solution: $\kvecx = \left[ \begin{smallmatrix} 1 \\ -2 \\ 1 \end{smallmatrix}\right] \bigl( a_1 \cos (\sqrt{{3k}/{m}}\, t) + b_1 \sin (\sqrt{{3k}/{m}}\, t) \bigr) + \left[ \begin{smallmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ -1 \end{smallmatrix}\right] \bigl( a_2 \cos (\sqrt{{k}/{m}}\, t) + b_2 \sin (\sqrt{{k}/{m}}\, t) \bigr) + \left[ \begin{smallmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \end{smallmatrix}\right] \bigl( a_3 t + b_3 \bigr).$

exercises.prompt: Suppose a cart of mass 2 kg is attached by a spring of constant $k=1$ to a cart of mass 3 kg, which is attached to the wall by a spring also of constant $k=1$. Suppose that the initial position of the first cart is 1 meter in the positive direction from the rest position, and the second cart starts at the rest position. The carts are not moving and are let go. Find the position of the second cart as a function of time.
